rounds.text: Scoobee Day Garments India Ltd presents a concerning financial profile characterized by persistent value destruction and operational instability. The company is currently generating negative returns, with ROE at -11.1% and ROCE at -6.1%, significantly underperforming sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E11, E12]. This poor performance is compounded by a severe contraction in top-line growth, evidenced by a 45% decline in compounded sales over the trailing twelve months and a 14% decline over the past three years [E14, E15]. Furthermore, the company’s profitability has collapsed, with compounded profit growth at -4891% over the trailing twelve months and a long-term trend of decreasing operating margins over the last five years [E17, E25]. The financial health is further pressured by a low interest coverage ratio and the potential capitalization of interest costs [E41, E44]. While the company has managed to maintain positive operating and free cash flow in the most recent fiscal year, its reliance on increasing borrowings—up to Rs 27.90 Cr from Rs 23.50 Cr—suggests an ongoing struggle to fund operations internally [E28, E29, E31]. Conceded: the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.30x and has seen a recent improvement in quarterly operating margins [E24, E30].

The bear focuses on historical trailing metrics, ignoring the clear evidence of a structural turnaround currently underway. While the bear cites negative ROE and ROCE [E8, E9, E11, E12], it overlooks the most recent quarterly data showing a massive 40 percentage point improvement in operating margins compared to the year-ago quarter [E24]. Conceded: the company has faced significant historical sales and profit declines [E14, E15, E17]. However, the most recent screening data highlights a sharp reversal, with sales up 80% and net profit up 65% year-over-year [E46, E48]. The bear’s concern regarding debt is contradicted by the company’s ability to generate Rs 6.19 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 5.83 Cr in free cash flow as of March 2026 [E28, E29]. Furthermore, the increase in borrowings [E31] is mitigated by the fact that the company maintains a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.30x [E30]. Finally, the bear ignores the strong signal of management confidence, as promoters have increased their stake to 79.75% [E33], suggesting they see value that the current, depressed share price does not reflect [E4, E40].

The bull’s reliance on a "structural turnaround" is premature given that the company’s long-term trajectory remains deeply negative, with compounded sales growth over three years at -14% [E14] and trailing twelve-month sales growth at -45% [E15]. While the bull highlights a quarterly margin improvement [E24], this follows a five-year trend of decreasing operating margins [E25] and a catastrophic -4891% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E17]. Conceded: the company generated positive operating and free cash flow in March 2026 [E28, E29]. However, this does not negate the fact that the company still suffers from a low interest coverage ratio [E41] and potential capitalization of interest costs [E44], which casts doubt on the quality of those earnings. Furthermore, the bull’s focus on promoter stake [E33] ignores that domestic institutional interest is actively declining [E34]. Ultimately, the company’s return on equity remains poor at -11.1% [E12], and the stock’s 14% position in its 52-week range [E4] reflects a persistent lack of market confidence that a single quarter of data has yet to reverse.
